section.title: Measurements
section.description: Enter tape measurements using the U.S. Navy circumference method. Results are approximate population-level estimates, not a medical diagnosis.

errors.range: Height should be between 100 and 250 cm.

heightImperial.label: Height
heightImperial.help: Feet and inches, standing without shoes.

errors.integer: Use a whole number for feet.
errors.combinedRange: Combined height should be between about 3 ft 4 in and 8 ft 2 in.
Combined height should be between about 3 ft 4 in and 8 ft 2 in.

neckCm.label: Neck
neckCm.help: Narrowest circumference below the larynx (Adam's apple), tape horizontal.

errors.range: Neck should be between 25 and 55 cm.

neckIn.label: Neck
neckIn.help: Narrowest point below the larynx, tape horizontal.

errors.range: Neck should be between 10 and 22 in.

abdomenCm.label: Abdomen (at navel)
abdomenCm.help: Horizontal tape at the navel, relaxed (do not suck in).

errors.range: Abdomen should be between 55 and 200 cm.
Abdomen should be between 22 and 79 in.

waistCm.label: Waist (narrowest)
waistCm.help: Narrowest horizontal circumference, usually near the natural waist.

errors.range: Waist should be between 50 and 180 cm.
Waist should be between 20 and 71 in.
Hip should be between 60 and 220 cm.
Hip should be between 24 and 87 in.

geometry.abdomenNeck: Abdomen must be greater than neck for this formula.
geometry.waistHipNeck: Waist plus hip must be greater than neck.

errors.unrealisticResult: Those measurements produce an unrealistic body fat estimate. Double-check tape placement and values.

status.empty: Fill in the fields to see an estimate.
status.incomplete: Complete the highlighted fields to continue.

section.title: Estimate
section.description: Body fat percentage from the Navy tape method. Categories are rough fitness-reference bands, not clinical cutoffs.

empty.body: Enter valid measurements and tap Estimate.

categories.obeseMale: Above typical fitness range (male reference band)
categories.obeseFemale: Above typical fitness range (female reference band)

messages.essentialMale: Roughly in the essential-to-very-lean band often cited for men; individual health varies.
messages.athleticMale: Roughly in the athletic band often cited for men.
messages.fitnessMale: Roughly in the fitness band often cited for men.
messages.averageMale: Roughly in the average band often cited for men.
messages.obeseMale: Roughly above the average band often cited for men; this is not a diagnosis.
messages.essentialFemale: Roughly in the essential band often cited for women.
messages.athleticFemale: Roughly in the athletic band often cited for women.
messages.fitnessFemale: Roughly in the fitness band often cited for women.
messages.averageFemale: Roughly in the average band often cited for women.
messages.obeseFemale: Roughly above the average band often cited for women; this is not a diagnosis.

disclaimer.title: Educational use
disclaimer.body: This tool uses a published circumference formula for approximation only. It is not medical advice and may differ from lab or clinical methods.

method.title: How measurements work
method.description: Follow the same landmarks the Navy method specifies so the estimate stays comparable to reference tables.

points.male: Men: neck (narrowest below the larynx), abdomen horizontal at the navel (relaxed), and standing height.
points.female: Women: neck, narrowest waist, widest hip/buttock circumference, and standing height.
points.navy: The calculation is the standard logarithmic U.S. Navy body fat estimation from those circumferences (measurements converted to inches internally).
points.categories: Category labels are simplified reference bands from common fitness charts; they are not enlistment or medical standards.

footer.disclaimer: For education only. If you have health concerns, speak with a qualified professional.
